messages:
jamie: FYI — after the RBAC role change to `app_reader` some users report 403 when hitting the internal app. Quick look shows SAML assertions for affected users missing the `groups` attribute. Anyone seen this pattern?

alicia: seeing the same. SCIM provisioning logs show successful 200 from Okta but our provisioner logs a KMS decrypt failure for those users' external_id, so they get deprovisioned locally. snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z ERROR scim-provisioner decrypt AccessDeniedException arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 user=alice@example.com external_id=null
```

mohit: did we rotate the KMS alias `alias/prod/scim` last week? tagging @sre-bot to check deploys and key policy changes. Could be key policy removed `kms:Decrypt` for the EC2/IAM role the provisioner uses.

sre-bot: deploy: 21987 applied 2026-03-17T02:07:12Z — infra-change: KMS key policy update (PR #482).

dena: if groups are missing our RBAC service falls back to SCIM external_id -> decrypt -> group lookup. If decrypt fails it drops to 'unassigned', hence access break. Short-term we should fallback to NameID/email mapping to preserve access until KMS is fixed.

jamie: mitigation plan: 1) add temporary RBAC policy to match on SAML NameID when `groups` absent (24h grace), 2) revert Okta NameID mapping if it changed, 3) fix KMS key policy and re-run SCIM sync. I'll open a quick ticket.

alicia: creating ticket <https://rwd/SEC-4587|SEC-4587> and will apply the RBAC patch now. Also starting a bulk SCIM re-sync for affected orgs after KMS fix.

mohit: confirmed: KMS alias rotated and new key id has a key policy that only grants `kms:Decrypt` to specific role ARN that doesn't include our `scim-provisioner` role. PR ready to update key policy and IAM role binding (https://git.rwd/pr/5123). Pushing fix now.

jamie: also noticed NameID format variance — our SP expects `urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent` but Okta is sending email format for a subset of users. That can cause account mismatch even if groups present. Check Okta mapping: `user.login` -> NameID was changed last week?

okta-bot: Okta app "redwood-internal": 29 assertions in last 24h with NameID=email. Mapping change by sarah@example.com at 2026-03-16T14:05:21Z.

dena: action list (owners): 1) revert Okta mapping to persistent (alicia), 2) update KMS key policy and IAM (mohit), 3) run SCIM bulk resync + monitor (alicia), 4) deploy temporary RBAC patch (jamie). ETA 3 hours. :white_check_mark:

alicia: applying RBAC patch now (PATCH to /rbac/policies/temporary). Will post when active.

jamie: RBAC patch applied. Temporary rules active and user stream shows users regaining access. Waiting on mohit to merge the key policy change.

mohit: PR merged, key policy updated, re-running failed decrypts. log: 
```
2026-03-18T10:03:12Z INFO scim-provisioner decrypt OK keyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/ef01-2345 user=alice@example.com external_id=usr-9832
```

dena: good. once SCIM resync completes we'll remove the temporary RBAC patch and close SEC-4587. I'll draft a short postmortem and add regression tests to CI to assert NameID format + KMS key policy bindings for the scim role.

jamie: noted — SEC-4587 update: resolution summary: reverted Okta NameID mapping, fixed KMS key policy + IAM binding, applied temporary RBAC fallback for 6h (removed after SCIM resync), created monitoring alert for missing `groups` in SAML assertions and for KMS decrypt error spikes. Closing this thread. :thumbsup:
